question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta / Fort William — Location]
options: Calcutta — Located on the eastern coast of India, on the banks of the Hooghly River
Calcutta — Situated in the Bengal region, present-day West Bengal
Fort William — English fort built at Calcutta on the Coromandel coast
Calcutta — Connected to the Bay of Bengal via the Hooghly River
wrong_fact: Fort William at Calcutta is NOT on the Coromandel coast. It is in Bengal, on the Hooghly River (a distributary of the Ganges), opening into the Bay of Bengal via a deltaic route. The Coromandel coast is the southeastern coast (Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh).
explanation: Calcutta (Kolkata) is in Bengal, in the Gangetic delta. Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690, and the village of Calcutta was formally established. Fort William was built there (named after King William III of England). The Hooghly River — a distributary of the Ganges — provides access to the Bay of Bengal. The Coromandel coast refers to the southeastern coast of India where Madras and Masulipatnam are located.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta / Fort William — Key Facts]
options: Job Charnock — English factor credited with founding Calcutta in 1690
Fort William — Named after King William III of England
Sutanuti, Govindpur, Kalikata — Three villages amalgamated to form Calcutta
Calcutta — Founded in 1661 when the English Crown granted trading rights to the Company
wrong_fact: Calcutta was NOT founded in 1661. Job Charnock established the English settlement at Sutanuti in 1690, not 1661. The year 1661 is associated with Bombay being received as a dowry.
explanation: Job Charnock arrived at the site of modern Calcutta in 1690, settling at the village of Sutanuti. The English later obtained the zamindari rights over three villages — Sutanuti, Govindpur, and Kalikata — from the Mughal government. Fort William was subsequently built and named after King William III. The year 1661 is significant for Bombay, not Calcutta. The amalgamation of the three villages into 'Calcutta' and the formal fortification came in the early 18th century.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta — Historical Events]
options: Black Hole of Calcutta (1756) — Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah captured Fort William and imprisoned English prisoners
Battle of Plassey (1757) — Fought near Calcutta on the banks of the Bhagirathi-Hooghly River
Robert Clive — Recaptured Calcutta from Siraj-ud-Daulah in January 1757
Calcutta — Became the capital of British India only after the Partition of Bengal (1905)
wrong_fact: Calcutta became the capital of British India in 1773 (with Warren Hastings as the first Governor-General), NOT after the Partition of Bengal in 1905. The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.
explanation: Calcutta served as the capital of British India from 1773 (under Warren Hastings, following the Regulating Act) until 1911 when King George V announced the transfer of the capital to Delhi (New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931). The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was a separate administrative event under Lord Curzon. The Black Hole incident (1756) and Battle of Plassey (1757) are correctly described — Siraj-ud-Daulah captured Fort William, and Clive recaptured Calcutta in early 1757.
